candidates.exact_span: 4Q3   Lowest four-day average flow rate expected to occur once every three-years
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines a specific low-flow statistic; if permit limits or monitoring conditions are keyed to 4Q3, different readings of 'four-day average' or 'once every three-years' could change which flow regime applies and thus which numeric limits or monitoring obligations are in effect.

candidates.exact_span: BOD   Biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies that BOD is five-day by default but allows other variants when noted; ambiguity about whether a given limit or measurement refers to five-day BOD versus another BOD basis could change which numeric limit applies and whether a reported value is comparable.

Defines BMP as a 'plan' rather than the more common 'practices'; if permit monitoring obligations are conditioned on BMP implementation or documentation, interpreting this term as a formal plan versus operational practices could change whether associated monitoring is required.

candidates.exact_span: ug/L       Micrograms per litter (one part per billion)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the mass/volume unit for trace pollutant limits; the misspelling 'litter' versus 'liter' could affect unit interpretation and thus whether reported measurements are in the same units as enforceable limits.

candidates.exact_span: mg/L  Milligrams per liter (one part per million)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the primary concentration unit used for effluent limits; a different unit reading or conversion assumption would change numeric compliance comparisons for reported measurements.

Introduces minimum quantification level as a reporting threshold; different interpretations of whether results below MQL are quantifiable for limit comparison versus treated as missing/non-numeric evidence could change exceedance determinations and missing-evidence classification.

Specifies that pH limits are expressed in standard units; ambiguity about how pH standard units are measured or compared to reported values could change whether a pH measurement exceeds the applicable limit.

References critical dilution as a defined concept; if permit limits are derived using dilution-based calculations, different interpretations of critical dilution could change the enforceable numeric limit applied to a discharge.

Defines reasonable potential, which in NPDES practice can trigger more stringent limits or additional monitoring; uncertainty about whether RP findings apply could change which numeric limits are enforceable and which monitoring requirements are in effect.

Defines DMR as the vehicle for discharge monitoring reporting; different interpretations of what constitutes a DMR submission or reporting period could change whether monitoring was required, was performed, or is documented versus missing.

Identifies effluent limitation guidelines as a limit source; if applicability of ELG-based limits is disputed, whether a parameter is governed by ELGs versus another limit basis could change the enforceable numeric limit used for comparison.

Distinguishes technology-based effluent limitations as a category of limits; uncertainty about whether a parameter's limit is TBEL-derived versus water-quality- or other-based could change which numeric limit applies.
Defines TMDL as a limit framework; if TMDL allocations govern a parameter, different interpretations of TMDL applicability could change the enforceable numeric discharge limit.

candidates.exact_span: NMWQS New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Waters
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies state water quality standards as a referenced standard set; if limits are derived from or compared to NMWQS, interpretation of which NMWQS criteria apply could change the applicable numeric limit.
